description: We are looking for aspiring programmer with space knowledge
summary:
EarthEcho is a zero-login web platform that turns NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band radar into plain-language answers about what changed on the ground, when it happened, and why—for any 6x6 place on Earth.

To address Dancing with the SARs, EarthEcho first reveals the "seasonal dance" of vegetation: using ESA WorldCover, it measures and removes each land-cover class's normal phenological swing in "HH" and "HV" backscatter so crop growth and monsoon green-up aren't mistaken for hazards. It then runs a Conradsen (2016) gamma likelihood-ratio change test—corrected for "HH-HV" correlation ( 0.5% false-alarm rate at α=0.01 ) and steep-slope radar shadow/layover—alongside NISAR L2 GUNW interferometric ground motion split into vertical and east–west components.

Instead of an unverified black-box AI label, each detected change polygon is fused with Copernicus DEM downhill routing (slope → river → road), NASA POWER rainfall, and OpenStreetMap infrastructure to rank 14 physical hypotheses with explicit evidence for, against, and a printable English/हिन्दी field-check sheet for local responders.
details:
What Does EarthEcho Do & How Does It Work?

EarthEcho turns raw NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data λ = 25 cm into tested, plain-language answers about what changed on the ground, when it happened, and why—for any 6 x 6 area on Earth, with no user login required.

When a user selects their location or one of 9 pre-computed global showcase sites (which open instantly, including Joshimath, Haridwar, Boone County, Corcoran, Kīlauea, Rondônia, and Kangerlussuaq) or clicks any new place on the map (analysed live in ~3 minutes), EarthEcho runs a 6-step scientific pipeline:

  1. Cloud-Native HDF5 Window Streaming: Instead of downloading multi-gigabyte granules, the backend queries the ASF DAAC API for the best-coverage NISAR track, filters out low-accuracy forecast orbits (orbit == "F"), and uses 8 parallel worker processes (fsspec + h5py) to stream only the exact 6 x 6 UTM pixel window from remote NISAR L2 GCOV (HH,HV backscatter at 20m) and L2 GUNW (unwrapped interferometric phase) HDF5 files in NASA Earthdata Cloud.
    • Using ESA WorldCover 10 m, EarthEcho computes the median seasonal trajectory for each land-cover class (e.g., cropland canopy growth vs. forest) and removes that regional phenological swing before testing for change—so seasons ≠ change.
    • Using Copernicus 30 m DEM slope/aspect and the satellite's look vector, steep slopes in radar layover or shadow are masked out.
    • Runs a per-pixel, per-date Gamma likelihood-ratio change-point test gated by the Conradsen et al. (2016) omnibus test at significance α=0.01, using local Equivalent Number of Looks (ENL).
    • Satterthwaite Correlation Correction: Because dual-pol HH and HV speckle are correlated (r̂), summing them naively inflates false alarms to 2.84%. EarthEcho scales the test statistic by c = 1 + r̂, keeping false alarms at 0.53% while detecting 100% of 3 dB changes ( 98.8%  dated to the exact 12-day pass) in Monte Carlo validation.
    • Reads NISAR L2 GUNW unwrapped phase, subtracts the ionospheric phase screen, masks low coherence (γ < 0.3) and 2π unwrapping jumps (>60mm), checks elevation correlation for tropospheric delay, and—when both ascending and descending tracks exist—solves the 2 x 2 viewing geometry to split motion into vertical (subsidence/heave) and east–west (slope creep) components.
    • Groups changed pixels into GeoJSON polygons, compares each polygon against a surrounding unchanged reference ring (ΔHΔHᵣₑ), and traces the steepest-descent downhill path over the DEM (Slope → River → Road) to see if debris or runoff reaches OpenStreetMap rivers or roads.
    • Evaluates each event against 14 physical hypotheses (flooding, sub-canopy inundation, landslide/debris flow, crop harvest, vegetation clearing, slow ground movement, freeze/thaw, etc.) using L-band scattering physics and 30-day NASA POWER rainfall, outputting an explicit Evidence Balance (Supporting, Contradicting, Cannot Test, and What Field/Optical Evidence Would Confirm It).

How Is the Project Creative?

  1. "Dancing with the SARs" Turned Into Both Science and Experience: We treat the rhythmic 12-day seasonal oscillation of crops, forests, and ice not just as a visualization (including Web Audio API radar sonification where users can hear canopy growth and sudden drops), but as a mathematical baseline that must be subtracted to find true anomalies.
  2. Epistemic Honesty Over Black-Box AI: Because no labeled NISAR change dataset exists yet, a trained ML classifier cannot be honestly validated. Instead, EarthEcho uses physics-based hypothesis ranking that explicitly tells the user what radar can and cannot prove.
  3. Full-Screen Story Mode (/#/story) & High-Contrast Change Map: Unchanged ground is dimmed while changed ground glows pink (brighter) or blue (darker); clicking any polygon zooms to it and snaps the before/after swipe to the exact NISAR pass dates before and after the event.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Zero-Barrier Access to NISAR: Citizens, journalists, agronomists, and district disaster officers never need a NASA Earthdata account, Python environment, or GIS software.
  • Actionable Field Readiness: Every detected event generates a transparent Monitoring Priority score (with inspectable weights) and a one-click Printable Field-Check Sheet with GPS coordinates, downhill river/road exposure, and confirmation checklists in English and हिन्दी (Hindi), plus a Simple / Expert toggle.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Uvicorn, asf_search, h5py + fsspec (HTTP byte-range cloud streaming), numpy, scipy (statistical distributions & morphology), rasterio + pyproj + shapely (COG warping & vector geometry), ProcessPoolExecutor (parallel HDF5 reads).
  • Frontend: React 18, Vite, MapLibre GL JS 5.6, Web Audio API (sonification), HTML5 Canvas.
  • NASA & Open Datasets: NASA–ISRO NISAR L2 GCOV & L2 GUNW (ASF DAAC), NASA GIBS WMTS daily mosaics, NASA POWER (PRECTOTCORR daily precipitation), Copernicus DEM GLO-30, ESA WorldCover 10 m, OpenStreetMap Overpass & Nominatim.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Scientific Validity & Self-Checking: Built a Monte Carlo speckle validation suite (validate_detector.py) that runs on startup so accuracy metrics shown in the UI always match the running code.
  • Honest Failure Modes: Automatically excludes inaccurate forecast-orbit granules, flags atmospheric phase delay when motion correlates with elevation ( r > 0.6), and distinguishes one-off latest-pass anomalies from changes confirmed across multiple passes.
  • Speed & Judge Experience: Bundled 9 pre-analysed global case studies for instant zero-wait exploration while optimizing live cloud analysis from 15 minutes down to ~3 minutes via multi-process HDF5 byte-range streaming.
